_about: A US residential brokerage, researched 17 Oct 2026 for Austin, TX (the first US profile, film-us.json). Market-wide facts live here; the metro's neighbourhoods, buildings and price index live in the profile. Every number names its source in _sources; a number marked ESTIMATE in _sources has none and is ours.

_sources.what: Phone numbers in 555-0100 to 555-0199 only: 'Only 555-0100 through 555-0199 are now specifically reserved for fictional use'
_sources.note: cites ATIS '555 NXX Line Number Reference Document' and NANPA '555 Line Numbers'; the NANPA/ATIS PDFs refused our fetch (403)

_sources.what: Out-of-town area codes and their weights (Texas metros, Bay Area, Chicago, New York): people who moved to Austin keep their numbers
_sources.note: ESTIMATE. Also forced by the fiction block: each area code has only 100 fictional numbers, so a few hundred contacts need about a dozen area codes

_sources.what: Name groups weighted 48 / 32 / 9 / 8 (white non-Hispanic, Hispanic or Latino, Asian, Black); QuickFacts Austin city: Hispanic 32.2%, White alone not Hispanic 47.6%, Black alone 7.5%, Asian alone 8.6%
_sources.note: read from search-result text; census.gov refused our fetch

_sources.what: Surnames: the 2010 Census frequently occurring surnames, top 40 by count (Smith 2,442,977 ... Flores 433,969)
_sources.note: ranks 11-40 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_common_surnames_in_North_America. Which group a surname is listed under, and the Asian surnames beyond the top 40 (Tran, Le, Pham, Patel, Kim, Chen, Wang, Singh), are our ESTIMATE

_sources.what: Given names: SSA Texas top 20 for births 1980-1989 and 1990-1999 (people now about 26 to 46, the age that buys and rents)
_sources.note: and https://namealmanac.com/state/TX/1990s; both built on the SSA state file. Splitting names across groups, and the Asian given names, are our ESTIMATE

_sources.what: Sources and weights. NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers: 43% of buyers found their agent by referral, 15% used an agent they had used before, 7% inquired about a property seen online, 7% were referred by another agent, 6% found the agent through a website, 5% met them at an open house; 52% of buyers found their home online
_sources.note: quoting NAR 2025; also https://store.realtor/2025-nar-profile-of-home-buyers-and-sellers-digital-download. The online share is split across portals in the order of their traffic (next source). The weights themselves are our ESTIMATE from these shares

_sources.what: Portal order: Comscore March 2024 monthly unique users Zillow 112M, Realtor.com 54M, Redfin 41M, Homes.com 39M
_sources.note: search-result text. Redfin is weighted low on purpose: it routes its buyers to its own and partner agents, so a small independent brokerage sees few. Apartments.com share: not found, ESTIMATE

_sources.what: Residential only: 'Although 70% of NAR members specialize primarily in residential brokerage'
Deposit one month's rent: Texas sets no cap; one month is the common deposit
_sources.note: a 2025 bill proposing a one-month cap; whether it passed was not confirmed

_sources.what: Fair housing: no 'family only' tenant preference on a listing
_sources.note: 42 U.S.C. 3604(c): no notice or advertisement indicating a preference based on familial status

_sources.what: Written buyer agreement before touring (NAR settlement, from 17 Aug 2024)
_sources.note: why the notes say 'signed buyer agreement' before a showing

_sources.what: Sizes in sq ft by bedrooms, baths by bedrooms, office hours 9:00 to 19:00 and no weekly day off (agents show homes at weekends)
_sources.note: ESTIMATE: no source found for any of these
